extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, accountants, auditors, and securities counsel preparing SEC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and interpretive guidance implementing disclosure requirements in Regulation S‑X and related SEC rules for climate-related impacts on financial statements, including thresholds, required line-item disaggregation, recoveries, and related GAAP/IFRS interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1% quantitative disclosure threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must disclose impacts when the aggregate amount of capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, or losses related to severe weather events and other natural conditions equals or exceeds 1% of the relevant denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules use income or loss before income tax expense or benefit and shareholders' equity or deficit as the denominators. The Commission expects many registrants will have insight into these denominators prior to fiscal-year-end, which should mitigate concerns about calculating the threshold only at year-end.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis thresholds ($100,000 / $500,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the 1% calculation yields an amount, disclosures are not required until aggregate amounts reach statutory de minimis floors: $100,000 for income-statement-related thresholds and $500,000 for balance-sheet-related thresholds (per the examples and Regulation S‑X precedent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If 1% of income before tax equals $50,000 (below $100,000), no disclosure required until aggregate expenditures/losses equal $100,000. If 1% of equity equals $250,000 (below $500,000), no balance-sheet disclosure required until aggregate capitalized costs/charges equal $500,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disaggregated financial statement line-item disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disaggregate and disclose amounts already recorded in the financial statements for any capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, or losses related to severe weather events and other natural conditions when the applicable threshold is met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosure is a disaggregation of amounts recognized in the financial statements (not a separate new accounting recognition). The Commission expects registrants to disclose aggregate amounts and to present the disclosure for the most recently completed fiscal year, and, to the extent previously disclosed or required, for historically presented fiscal years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of disclosed amounts (capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, losses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule requires disclosure of aggregate capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses that arise from severe weather events and other natural conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the final rules, charges (which would have been part of Financial Impact Metrics in the proposal) are included in the scope of required disclosure where applicable; the earlier Expenditure Metrics focused only on expenditures (spending).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution principle for costs (significant contributing factor rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a severe weather event or natural condition is a significant contributing factor to incurred costs, the registrant must disclose the entire cost incurred (subject to thresholds), even if other factors also contributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative example: if a tornado damages a roof and the registrant incurs repair costs, the tornado as a significant contributing factor requires disclosure of the full repair cost if the disclosure threshold is triggered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution principle applies to recoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: The attribution principle also applies to recoveries (e.g., insurance proceeds) associated with severe weather events and other natural conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must disclose aggregate recoveries recognized during the fiscal year for events for which they disclosed capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, or losses. Recoveries are not limited to insurance proceeds and can include guarantees or indemnifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recoveries disclosure and contextual information
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must separately disclose whether they have recognized any recoveries (such as insurance proceeds) as part of contextual information to help investors understand the financial-statement effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules do not prescribe how recoveries must be accounted for in the financial statements (registrants should follow GAAP). Registrants may provide additional disclosure to clarify instances where recoveries could create the impression that recoveries exceed expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of periods for expenditure metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The expenditure metrics (focused on spending incurred) should be reported for the number of years of the income statement or cash flow statement presented in the consolidated financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposing Release indicated the periods of the expenditure metrics should correspond to presented financial-statement periods; the final rules align disclosure periods with the consolidated financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of amounts recorded in financial statements (disaggregation basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The required climate-related disaggregations should be based on amounts recorded in the registrant's financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments (e.g., KPMG) recommended clarifying that disclosures are a disaggregation of already-recognized amounts; the Commission incorporated that approach in the final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign private issuer accounting basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign private issuers that file consolidated financial statements under home country GAAP and reconcile to U.S. GAAP must use U.S. GAAP (including the final rules) as the basis for calculating and disclosing the information; foreign private issuers that file under IFRS as issued by the IASB should apply IFRS and the final rules as the basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See references to Form 20‑F proposed amendments and the treatment of foreign private issuers in the final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with GAAP/IFRS accounting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must consider material climate-related matters when applying existing U.S. GAAP and IFRS accounting standards (e.g., ASC topics on inventory, impairment, contingencies, risks and uncertainties, segment reporting, equity method, consolidations, fair value measurement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission notes longstanding accounting guidance and educational materials reminding entities to report financial-statement effects of material climate-related matters (e.g., FASB and IFRS guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality and anti-misleading obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Even with a 1% rule, registrants retain the fundamental obligation not to make materially misleading statements or omissions and may need to provide additional information beyond the rule's thresholds to avoid misleading investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations include 17 CFR 230.408, 240.12b-20, and Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 99 emphasizing that percentage thresholds cannot substitute for materiality determinations required by accounting principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and examples of 'severe weather events and other natural conditions'
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules confirm examples of acute and chronic risks that qualify: acute examples include hurricanes, floods, tornadoes; chronic examples include sustained phenomena like sea level rise, drought, extreme temperatures and wildfires. The term 'severe' modifies both weather events and other natural conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final amendments to Regulation S‑X retain examples from the proposing release (flooding, drought, wildfires, extreme temperatures, sea level rise) and emphasize the 'severe' qualifier for Rule 14‑02 disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural conditions need not be climate-related; cause not required
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'natural conditions' that trigger disclosure need not be climate-related (e.g., can include earthquakes), and registrants are not required to determine the cause of a wildfire or other event for disclosure purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission clarifies that cause is irrelevant to determining whether disclosure is required under Rules 14‑01 and 14‑02; this simplifies registrants' analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial disclosure when thresholds triggered only for one statement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible that the disclosure threshold may be triggered for a registrant's balance sheet but not its income statement, or vice versa, resulting in only partial disclosure of capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses related to the events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants are required to disclose the aggregate amount of any recoveries recognized during the fiscal year for which costs/losses have been disclosed. Nothing prevents a registrant from voluntarily disclosing how an event affected both statements even if one threshold is not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rules do not adopt proposed Financial Impact Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is not adopting the proposed Financial Impact Metrics, and therefore registrants do not have the option to disclose impacts of climate-related opportunities on those Financial Impact Metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the same reason, the proposed requirement to include impacts of climate-related risks on the Financial Impact Metrics is not adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedent for percentage-based disaggregation in Regulation S‑X
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation S‑X and other securities law provisions include existing percentage thresholds requiring disaggregated disclosure (e.g., 1% rule for excise taxes; 5% rule for amounts in excess of total current assets), providing precedent for the Commission's 1% disclosure threshold approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited regulations include 17 CFR 210.5-03.1(a) and 17 CFR 210.5-02.8 as examples of percentage thresholds used elsewhere in reporting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples and comparability guidance to assist registrants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission provides examples of severe weather events and other natural conditions to aid comparability and assist issuers in making the disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing examples is intended to aid consistency across registrants' disclosures while assisting issuants in applying the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure should reflect amounts attributable to severe events even if routine accounting presents similar expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may need to distinguish climate-related or severe-event-driven costs from routine or discrete charges (e.g., excise taxes are discrete and knowable) and explain measurement where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted differences in ease of measuring certain items (e.g., excise taxes vs. climate impacts). The Commission acknowledges such measurement challenges and suggests use of existing accounting records and principles to identify and disaggregate amounts.
